finding: guard-human-fields starts one git process per word of an interpreter script. check_shell calls guarded for each path-like word of a heredoc body or a python3 -c text, and guarded runs git rev-parse each time. Measured on a scratch repository: 1500 words take 3.05 seconds and 5000 words take 11.27 seconds, on every such Bash call. The Copilot hook entry in guard-human-fields.json sets timeoutSec to 10. Fix: in check_shell, skip a word that does not contain docs/ before calling guarded, or keep the project root per directory.
why_this_severity: The guard decides correctly on these calls, and a short script costs well under a second (no to fails_purpose). A long agent script waits seconds on every call, and above about 4400 words it passes the 10-second limit of the Copilot entry.
